ops.body:
Design record — shipped across cc-transcript 10.5.0/10.6.0 and capt-hook 8.18.0 (wave b1fafa07..d26e4ada; family-level per the user's pick).

CHOSEN DESIGN (three layers):
1. Family-level relay marker (cc-transcript 10.5.0, 00b3978): parse-time `UserEvent.is_agent_injected`, computed from the existing AGENT_INJECTION_GROUPS filterspec regexes (single source; Rust parity in protocol.rs/event.rs/activity.rs). The "fragile wrapper prefix" concern resolved by hardening the spec instead of inventing a new marker: 10.6.0 (302ceba) anchored the patterns to start-of-text (a banner IS the message; mid-text mentions no longer classify) and replaced \b with portable follower classes after codex proved a Python-re-vs-Rust-regex combining-mark divergence, plus ASCII-pinned the Reminder 'i' against dotted/dotless-I folds. Deliberate scope expansion: injected banners also stop opening turns in BOTH backends' activity models including the is_waiting oracle (option A — keeps three-way classifier/probe/Rust parity; a banner is not the human speaking, so it no longer closes the pending-tool waiting window).
2. capt-hook exclusion (7a7c452c): transcript_texts drops is_agent_injected UserEvents from signal candidates unconditionally — relay digests quoting a hook's tells can never re-trigger it, cross-agent included.
3. Quote/echo damping (7a7c452c + e2531bb9): PrimitiveState.echo_verbatim seeds the fired warn MESSAGE's sentences only (whitespace-normalized, >=20-char floor, 40-entry FIFO, batch-deduped) — NEVER the matched excerpts (excerpts are the tells; seeding them would permanently mute the hook). Damping is strip-and-score, not drop-whole-candidate: seeded sentences are stripped and the remainder scored, so quoting the warn while re-offending still fires (codex-found refinement). Session-lifetime, global across hooks. EchoTracker forward horizon fixed from a flat 5 to ECHO_WINDOW + (int window | TURN_ECHO_LOOKBACK=40) — a SUM, covering parrot-writes reachable by the hook's own lookback.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES:
- Cross-session decisions-ledger containment query at match time: rejected on per-event query cost and scoping policy (which sessions' warns should mute this one?).
- Decoupling probe_events from native_user_classifier to keep the oracle byte-identical: rejected — forks the turn-boundary definition per-consumer, the per-repo point-fix shape this family avoids.
- Tightening the NLP issue+leave clause: dropped by user pick; live-verified the clause wasn't the false-positive source.
- Seeding matched excerpts into the echo ledger: rejected (permanent hook muting — excerpts ARE the tells).

ACCEPTED RESIDUALS (fire-log watch items, not reopen triggers):
- An orchestrator PARAPHRASING (not quoting >=20 verbatim chars of) a warn fired in a subagent's session can still trigger cross-session; escape hatch if it materializes: SessionStart seed of echo_verbatim from the decisions ledger (kind=hook_name, message column) — designed, not built.
- Excerpt-only quotes beyond the echo horizon still score (relays are covered by the marker; assistant self-quotes of raw tells without the warn sentence are not).
- A candidate that is a pure warn-quote is damped even if a hook would legitimately re-warn.

Fire-log evidence pre-fix: 10+ relay fires incl. session 0f339270's recon digests tripping stewardship and typing-warnings on verbatim tells; EchoTracker's flat 5-event window vs window=15 lookback proven leaky by the fire+8 paraphrase red test.
